module

public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Infinite

public section

lemma Nat.exists_prime_not_dvd {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ ¬p ∣ n := by
  let ⟨p, hnp, hp⟩ := (n + 1).exists_infinite_primes
  exact ⟨p, hp, not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt (by lia) (by lia)⟩

status_issues.source_status: Erdős Problem 457 is solved affirmatively and verified in Lean. The source credits a construction by GPT-5.2 Pro prompted by Kevin Barreto, and explicitly identifies the q-formulation with this problem. The source page was last edited 7 March 2026.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/457: “PROVED (LEAN)” and “This has been solved in the affirmative and the proof verified in Lean.” Its discussion states that the problem asks whether q(n, log n) ≥ (2 + ε) log n infinitely often. The equivalence with the primary statement was independently checked in Lean.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change this variant to category research solved and replace answer(sorry) with answer(True). Its solution follows from the already-solved primary declaration via the checked equivalence.

reformulations.difference: The caller's variant replaces the source's primary condition that every prime p ≤ (2 + ε) log n divides the product with the non-strict bound (2 + ε) log n ≤ q(n, log n). The source also explicitly presents this q-formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: By minimality of q, divisibility by every prime p ≤ B is equivalent to B < q. Thus the primary condition implies the q-variant with the same ε. Conversely, given the q-variant with ε > 0, discard n = 0,1 and replace ε by ε/2. Then log n > 0 and (2 + ε/2) log n < (2 + ε) log n ≤ q, giving the primary divisibility condition on an infinite subset. Both the threshold equivalence and the equivalence of the quantified statements were proved in /workspace/review/use_site.lean without relying on sorry-proved problem statements.

review.notes: No mathematical defect found. The file contains only Nat.exists_prime_not_dvd and introduces no definitions. Lean experiments proved that its existential conclusion holds exactly when n ≠ 0, checked small witnesses, and confirmed that Nat.find selects the least nondividing prime rather than the larger witness constructed in the lemma's proof. The sole caller, Erdos457.q, has a nonzero product for every permitted input; its floor-indexed interval and empty-product cases agree with the source. The upper-bound variant matches the still-open problem 1181. Both scratch files compiled successfully. No repository files were edited; the target matches the specified commit.
